title: Module objects over a commutative monoid are symmetric bimodules
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category with braiding $\beta$, and let
$\mathcal R$ be a commutative monoid object of $\mathcal C$. Let $M$ be an
$\mathcal R$-module object ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]). Then the left action $\gamma_M$
and the right action
$$
\rho_M:=\gamma_M\circ\beta_{M,\mathcal R}\colon M\otimes\mathcal R\to M
$$
make $M$ an $\mathcal R$-$\mathcal R$-bimodule. Call a bimodule *symmetric* if its right
action is the braiding followed by its left action. The functor
$M\mapsto(M,\gamma_M,\rho_M)$ from $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ to
$\mathcal R$-$\mathcal R$-bimodules is fully faithful, and its values are symmetric
bimodules.

proof.text:
Write $R=\mathcal R$, $a=\gamma_M$ and $r=a\circ\beta_{M,R}$. All compositions below use ordinary right-to-left order; $\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$, and $\varrho$ denotes the right unitor, distinct from the action $r$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects],
$$a\circ(\eta\otimes M)=\lambda_M,\qquad a\circ(R\otimes a)=a\circ(\mu\otimes M)\circ\alpha_{R,R,M}^{-1}.$$
The five laws in [def-sfb-bimod-objects] specialize to these two left action laws, the right unit law, the right associative law and the middle compatibility law. Thus the left laws are already satisfied; the next three steps verify the other three for the specified morphism $r$.

source.place: First paragraph: the left module supplies the left action; define the right action.

proof.text:
Naturality of the braiding [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality], with $f=\mathrm{id}_M$ and $g=\eta:\mathbf 1\to R$, and the left module unit law [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] give
$$r\circ(M\otimes\eta)=a\circ\beta_{M,R}\circ(M\otimes\eta)=a\circ(\eta\otimes M)\circ\beta_{M,\mathbf 1}=\lambda_M\circ\beta_{M,\mathbf 1}=\varrho_M.$$
The last equality is [lem-sfb-braiding-unitors]. This is precisely the right unit law.

source.place: First paragraph: right unit and braiding with the monoidal unit.

proof.text:
For compatibility, naturality [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality] applied to $a:R\otimes M\to M$ and $\mathrm{id}_R$, the left module associativity [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and the first formula of [lem-sfb-braiding-hexagon] with $(X,Y,Z)=(R,M,R)$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
r\circ(a\otimes R)
&=a\circ(R\otimes a)\circ\beta_{R\otimes M,R}\\
&=a\circ(\mu\otimes M)\circ\alpha_{R,R,M}^{-1}\circ\beta_{R\otimes M,R}\\
&=a\circ((\mu\circ\beta_{R,R})\otimes M)\circ\alpha_{R,R,M}^{-1}\circ(R\otimes\beta_{M,R})\circ\alpha_{R,M,R}\\
&=a\circ(\mu\otimes M)\circ\alpha_{R,R,M}^{-1}\circ(R\otimes\beta_{M,R})\circ\alpha_{R,M,R}\\
&=a\circ(R\otimes a)\circ(R\otimes\beta_{M,R})\circ\alpha_{R,M,R}
=a\circ(R\otimes r)\circ\alpha_{R,M,R}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line cancels the adjacent inverse associators after expanding the hexagon. The fourth line uses exactly $\mu\circ\beta_{R,R}=\mu$, the definition of commutativity in [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]. Tensor functoriality and the definition of $r$ give the final equality. This proves the middle compatibility law, without assuming that the braiding is symmetric.

source.place: First paragraph: compatibility of left and right actions from naturality, hexagon and commutativity.

proof.text:
For right associativity, the compatibility just proved in step 3 and tensor functoriality give
$$\begin{aligned}
r\circ(r\otimes R)
&=r\circ(a\otimes R)\circ(\beta_{M,R}\otimes R)\\
&=a\circ(R\otimes a)\circ(R\otimes\beta_{M,R})\circ\alpha_{R,M,R}\circ(\beta_{M,R}\otimes R).
\end{aligned}$$
On the other hand, naturality [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality] with $\mathrm{id}_M,\mu$, and the second formula of [lem-sfb-braiding-hexagon] with $(X,Y,Z)=(M,R,R)$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
r\circ(M\otimes\mu)\circ\alpha_{M,R,R}
&=a\circ(\mu\otimes M)\circ\beta_{M,R\otimes R}\circ\alpha_{M,R,R}\\
&=a\circ(\mu\otimes M)\circ\alpha_{R,R,M}^{-1}\circ(R\otimes\beta_{M,R})\circ\alpha_{R,M,R}\circ(\beta_{M,R}\otimes R)\\
&=a\circ(R\otimes a)\circ(R\otimes\beta_{M,R})\circ\alpha_{R,M,R}\circ(\beta_{M,R}\otimes R).
\end{aligned}$$
Here the second equality cancels the final $\alpha_{M,R,R}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{M,R,R}$ from the hexagon, and the third uses the left module associativity [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. The two calculations have the same last composite, so $r\circ(r\otimes R)=r\circ(M\otimes\mu)\circ\alpha_{M,R,R}$. Together with steps 1-3 this supplies all five bimodule laws of [def-sfb-bimod-objects].

source.place: First paragraph: right associativity from naturality and hexagon; use compatibility proved in step 3.

proof.text:
Let $f:M\to N$ be a left module morphism. Its defining equation [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and braiding naturality [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality] give
$$\begin{aligned}
f\circ r_M&=f\circ\gamma_M\circ\beta_{M,R}
=\gamma_N\circ(R\otimes f)\circ\beta_{M,R}\\
&=\gamma_N\circ\beta_{N,R}\circ(f\otimes R)
=r_N\circ(f\otimes R).
\end{aligned}$$
Thus $f$ preserves both actions and is a bimodule morphism [def-sfb-bimod-objects]. The assignment on morphisms is its underlying morphism $f$; identities and composition are preserved because both categories inherit them from $\mathcal C$. Conversely, a bimodule morphism between the constructed bimodules preserves the left action, hence defines a left module morphism. These two operations on hom-sets are inverse: both keep the underlying morphism, which determines a morphism in either category. Hence each hom-set map is bijective and the functor is fully faithful. Each value is symmetric because its right action was defined as $\gamma_M\circ\beta_{M,R}$.

source.place: Second paragraph: functoriality, both directions on hom-sets, full faithfulness and symmetry.

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; expanded action-law calculations with all associators written.
